job.title: Qualified Carpenter
job.description:
Step into a busy Wellington construction environment where your qualified carpentry skills will be put to full use on a variety of residential and commercial projects.
This fixed-term role offers the chance to work on well-managed sites with clear plans, quality materials, and a strong focus on workmanship and safety.

About the Role:
You will be responsible for delivering high-quality carpentry work from structural framing through to detailed finishing, ensuring all tasks are completed to specification and within agreed timeframes.
Working closely with site supervisors and other trades, you’ll contribute to the successful delivery of builds that meet New Zealand standards.
Your accuracy and attention to detail will help ensure projects are completed correctly the first time.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Read and interpret construction drawings, plans, and specifications to determine project requirements.
  • Measure, cut, and shape timber and other materials for structural and finishing work.
  • Install framing, joists, rafters, and roof structures in line with project specifications.
  • Carry out accurate site set-out, levelling, and alignment for structural components.
  • Construct and install cabinetry, fittings, doors, windows, and interior trim to a high standard.
  • Use hand and power tools safely and efficiently to complete carpentry tasks.
  • Perform repairs and maintenance on existing structures as required.
  • Follow on-site health and safety procedures and contribute to maintaining a safe work environment.

Key Requirements:
  • Proven experience as a Qualified Carpenter in residential and/or commercial construction.
  • Strong ability to read and interpret construction plans and technical drawings.
  • Demonstrated competence in framing, roofing, and first-fix carpentry.
  • Solid experience with finishing work, including doors, windows, interior trim, and cabinetry installation.
  • Confident in accurate measuring, cutting, and site set-out.
  • Skilled in the safe and efficient use of a wide range of hand and power tools.
  • Sound knowledge of the New Zealand Building Code and relevant building standards.
  • Reliable, punctual, and able to work effectively as part of a site team.

Desirable Skills:
  • Experience working on both new builds and renovation projects.
  • Familiarity with commercial fit-out work and detailed joinery.
  • Ability to identify and resolve minor on-site issues with minimal supervision.
  • Exposure to working with a variety of building materials beyond timber.

Qualifications:
  • New Zealand trade qualification in carpentry (or equivalent recognised overseas qualification).
  • Current Site Safe or equivalent construction safety certification (or willingness to obtain).
  • Any additional construction or building-related certifications will be an advantage.


If you’re a Qualified Carpenter looking for a fixed-term role in Wellington where your skills will be valued and fully utilised, apply now to be considered.

job.title: Metal Fabricator/Welder
job.description:
Enterprise Recruitment is working alongside leaders in the manufacturing and maintenance service industry in New Zealand. Due to the continual growth in this market, our client - a New Zealand owned and operated manufacturing and maintenance service maintenance provider - is looking for 3 Metal Fabricators/Welders to join their growing team.

  • Perform arc & mig mild steel welding in a workshop environment
  • Read and interpret engineering drawings and dimensions
  • Work off site to install heavy and mild Steel  
  • Fabricate and repair metal products using a variety of welding techniques 
  • Create a variety of mild steel products in vertical ups, horizontal and overhead styles of welding
 
In addition to the above, the right candidate must be able to perform the following tasks: 
  • Studying blueprints, drawings and specifications to determine job requirements
  • Selecting, cleaning and preparing metal stock
  • Cutting marked-out metal sections and shapes using hand tools, flame cutting torches and metal cutting machines

  • Aligning parts to be joined using hand tools and measuring instruments
  • Joining metal sections using various welding techniques, bolting and riveting
  • Examining welds for width of bead, penetration and precision
  • Finishing products by cleaning, polishing, filing and bathing in acidic solutions
